item.title: Study: Earth can sustain only 2.5 billion people
item.description: The Earth can no longer sustain its current human population, according to a study published Monday in Environmental Research Letters by an international team of researchers. The paper concludes that the planet's sustainable carrying capacity is roughly 2.5 billion people — less than a third of today's 8.3 billion — and that decades of fossil fuel dependence have masked the true scale of ecological overshoot.

item.title: Iran denies direct talks with U.S. as Trump claims deal is close
item.description: President Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday that U.S.-Iran negotiations were going "extremely well" through both direct and indirect channels, claiming a deal to end the war could come soon. But Iran flatly denied any direct engagement, and the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee accused Trump of fabricating the talks to stabilize rattled financial markets.

item.title: Tanker struck near Dubai as Gulf attacks mount
item.description: An unknown projectile struck a tanker approximately 31 nautical miles northwest of Dubai on Monday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, adding to a relentless series of attacks on commercial shipping that has upended global energy markets since the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran erupted on February 28.

item.title: Netanyahu says Iran war is 'beyond the halfway point'
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday that the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran has passed its midway mark, with the current focus shifting to securing or removing Iran's remaining stockpile of enriched uranium. The remarks came during an exclusive sit-down interview with Newsmax CEO Chris Ruddy in Jerusalem — Netanyahu's first in-depth interview since the war began on February 28.

Netanyahu described the mission as "beyond the halfway point" but declined to put a specific timeline on the conflict's conclusion, saying there is still "a lot more to do". He expressed confidence in the trajectory of the campaign, framing Iran as emerging weaker while the U.S.-Israel alliance grows stronger.

item.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's energy infrastructure if no deal reached
item.description:
President Trump on Monday threatened to "completely obliterate" Iran's electric generating plants, oil wells, and Kharg Island — and possibly its desalination plants — if a peace deal is not reached "shortly" and the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened, dramatically escalating his rhetoric as the war entered its 31st day.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that "The United States of America is in serious discussions with A NEW, AND MORE REASONABLE, REGIME to end our Military Operations in Iran," claiming "great progress" had been made. But he warned that absent a deal, "we will conclude our lovely 'stay' in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet 'touched'".

item.title: Zelensky says Russia exploiting Iran war to fund its fight against Ukraine
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Monday that a prolonged war in Iran is delivering outsized benefits to Russia while undermining Ukraine's security, telling Axios in an exclusive interview that Moscow is exploiting the Middle East conflict to boost its war economy and erode Western support for Kyiv.

"I am sure Russia wants long war. They have benefits: The U.S. is focusing on the Middle East and may decrease military help to Ukraine. Sanctions are partially lifted. I see only benefits for Russia from the war with Iran continuing," Zelensky said over Zoom after returning from a tour of Middle Eastern capitals.

item.title: Iran's parliament approves plan to toll ships in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's parliamentary security commission on Monday approved a plan to impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing a fee system that has been operating on an ad hoc basis since the outbreak of war in late February and setting up a likely flashpoint in ongoing peace negotiations with the United States.

item.title: Kuwaiti oil tanker hit by projectile near Dubai port
item.description:
A fully loaded Kuwaiti crude oil tanker was struck by a projectile while anchored near Dubai port early on Tuesday, March 31, sparking a fire onboard and raising fears of an oil spill in the Persian Gulf, according to Kuwait's state news agency and a British maritime monitoring authority.

Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said the very large crude carrier Al Salmi was "directly targeted in what it described as an Iranian attack while in the anchorage area of Dubai Port in the United Arab Emirates," the state news agency KUNA reported, as cited by Reuters. The corporation warned of a possible oil spill in surrounding waters, adding that the tanker was fully loaded at the time of the strike. No crew casualties were reported, and emergency response and firefighting teams were mobilized to contain the situation.

item.title: NYU closes Abu Dhabi campus after Iran threatens US universities
item.description:
New York University has temporarily shut down its Abu Dhabi campus after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared American university outposts in the Middle East "legitimate targets" for retaliation, marking a sharp escalation that extends the ongoing conflict into the realm of civilian academic institutions.

The closure, announced on Monday, suspends physical access to the campus for all students, faculty, and staff, with classes continuing remotely, according to NYU's student newspaper, Washington Square News. The university said the decision was made "out of an abundance of caution" following the IRGC's threat on Sunday.

item.title: Iran says ambassador will stay in Beirut despite Lebanon's expulsion order
item.description:
Iran on Monday openly refused to comply with Lebanon's order to expel its ambassador, declaring that the envoy would remain in Beirut and continue his duties — a direct challenge to the Lebanese government's authority that has deepened a diplomatic crisis at the heart of the broader regional conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei confirmed at a news conference that Ambassador Mohammad Reza Shibani had no plans to leave. "Our embassy is open and our ambassador continues his work in Beirut and remains present," Baghaei said, according to Iran International. The statement came one day after a March 29 deadline set by Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi for Shibani to depart the country.

item.title: US struck Isfahan ammo depot with bunker busters
item.description:
The United States struck a large ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan with a high volume of 2,000-pound penetrator munitions, according to a U.S. official cited by The Wall Street Journal. The strike triggered a chain of secondary explosions that lit up the night sky, with footage of towering fireballs circulating widely after President Trump shared an uncaptioned video of the attack on his Truth Social platform on Sunday evening. The Wall Street Journal confirmed the footage depicted the Isfahan operation.

The strike is the latest in more than a month of sustained U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, launched on February 28 under what the Israel Defense Forces have termed "Operation Roaring Lion". Since then, more than 15,000 Iranian targets have been hit, according to the IDF, with the daily strike tempo declining from roughly 1,000 targets in the opening days to fewer than 100.

item.title: Trump willing to end Iran war without reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump has told aides he is willing to conclude the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial shipping, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, a move that could leave Tehran with lasting leverage over one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.

The shift signals a recalibration of American war aims as the conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, enters its fifth week. In recent discussions, Trump and his advisers concluded that attempting to force the strait open would extend the fighting beyond his preferred four-to-six-week timeline, according to administration officials cited by the Journal. Instead, Washington plans to focus on its stated objectives — degrading Iran's naval and missile capabilities — while pursuing diplomatic channels to persuade Tehran to restore maritime traffic.

item.title: Asian nations rush to buy Russian crude as Iran war chokes oil supply
item.description:
A growing number of Asian countries are turning to Russia for crude oil as the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran continues to choke off energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."

The Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka have all signaled interest in purchasing Russian crude in recent weeks, joining established buyers China and India in a regional competition for barrels that analysts warn may soon outstrip what Moscow can deliver.

item.title: Data centers warm nearby land by up to 16°F, Cambridge study finds
item.description: The sprawling data centers powering artificial intelligence are creating localized "heat islands" that raise surface temperatures by an average of 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit — and up to 16.4 degrees in extreme cases — affecting an estimated 340 million people worldwide, according to new research from the University of Cambridge.

item.title: Gold climbs on report Trump may end Iran war
item.description: Gold prices climbed on Monday after a Wall Street Journal report that President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the U.S. military campaign against Iran, even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. The gains extended into early Asian trading on Tuesday, with the metal also buoyed by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's comments at Harvard University that eased fears of an imminent interest rate hike.

item.title: Australia, Indonesia probe tech giants over under-16 bans
item.description: Australia and Indonesia are both cracking down on major technology companies this week for failing to enforce new laws banning children under 16 from social media, in a coordinated global push to hold platforms accountable for youth safety online.

item.title: Global banks turn to Chinese stocks as Iran war roils markets
item.description: As the month-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran roils global markets and sends oil prices soaring, Chinese equities — and the country's dominant renewable energy sector in particular — have emerged as a rare bright spot for investors seeking refuge from the turmoil.

item.title: Hegseth calls upcoming days 'decisive' in Iran war
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday described the "upcoming days" as decisive in the month-long U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, pointing to widespread desertions within Tehran's armed forces and the degradation of its military capabilities as signs that the conflict is approaching a turning point.

item.title: Trump tells allies to 'take' Strait of Hormuz themselves
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his pressure on reluctant allies on Tuesday, posting on Truth Social that countries struggling with jet fuel shortages caused by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz should either purchase American oil or seize control of the waterway themselves.

"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you: Number 1, buy from the US, we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT," Trump wrote, singling out nations that declined to join U.S. strikes against Iran. He added that the United States "won't be there to help you anymore" and that allies would need to learn "how to fight for yourself".

item.title: U.S., Israel strike Isfahan and Tehran on Day 32 of Iran war
item.description: As the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran entered its 32nd day on Tuesday, powerful explosions rocked both Tehran and the central city of Isfahan in what appeared to be some of the most intense aerial bombardments since hostilities began on February 28. The escalation came alongside fresh Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region and a parallel diplomatic push led by Pakistan to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.
